import pandas as pd

# File paths for source data
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_47/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_47/training_1.csv"

# Step 1: Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation History:
# ['UNPIVOT', 
#  'JOIN : [["Source3_47_0","Source3_47_1"],["Country Name","Country Name"],["Country Code","Country Code"]]', 
#  'UNPIVOT', 
#  'JOIN : [["Source3_47_0","Source3_47_1"],["Country Name","Country Name"],["Country Code","Country Code"]]']

# === First UNPIVOT on Source3_47_0 ===
# Unpivot year columns (1960-2017) into 'Year' and 'Rural Value' columns
year_cols = [str(y) for y in range(1960, 2018)]
df0_unpivot = df0.melt(
    id_vars=['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Indicator Name', 'Indicator Code'],
    value_vars=year_cols,
    var_name='Year',
    value_name='Rural Value'
)

# Filter df0_unpivot to keep only rows where Indicator Name corresponds to Rural population
# According to source0 example, Rural population indicator name is "Rural population (% of total population)"
df0_unpivot = df0_unpivot[df0_unpivot['Indicator Name'] == "Rural population (% of total population)"].copy()

# Drop Indicator Code and Indicator Name as they are no longer needed
df0_unpivot.drop(columns=['Indicator Name', 'Indicator Code'], inplace=True)

# === First JOIN between Source3_47_0 and Source3_47_1 ===
# Before join, we need to unpivot Source3_47_1 as well, but operation history says UNPIVOT after join,
# so we join first on the original df0_unpivot and df1 (not unpivoted yet).

# But operation history is strict: UNPIVOT, then JOIN, then UNPIVOT, then JOIN.
# So after first UNPIVOT on Source3_47_0, join with Source3_47_1 (still pivoted).

# To join, we need to align keys and year columns.
# df0_unpivot has columns: Country Name, Country Code, Year, Rural Value
# df1 has columns: Country Name, Country Code, Indicator Name, Indicator Code, 1960..2017

# We join on Country Name and Country Code, but year is still pivoted in df0_unpivot and wide in df1.
# To join properly, we need to unpivot df1 after join according to operation history.

# So first join df0_unpivot with df1 on Country Name and Country Code, but year is not a join key yet.
# We must join on Country Name and Country Code only, then unpivot df1.

# To join df0_unpivot with df1, we need to replicate df1 rows for each year in df0_unpivot or vice versa.
# But operation history says join on Country Name and Country Code only.

# The best approach is to join df0_unpivot with df1 on Country Name and Country Code,
# then unpivot df1 after join.

# To do this, we merge df0_unpivot with df1 on Country Name and Country Code (many-to-many join),
# then unpivot the joined df1 part.

# Perform join:
df_join1 = pd.merge(
    df0_unpivot,
    df1,
    on=['Country Name', 'Country Code'],
    how='inner',
    suffixes=('_rural', '_elec')
)

# === Second UNPIVOT on Source3_47_1 part of the joined dataframe ===
# The columns to unpivot in df1 are year columns 1960-2017
# We unpivot these columns into 'Year' and 'Electricity Value'

# The joined dataframe has columns:
# ['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Rural Value', 'Indicator Name', 'Indicator Code', '1960', ..., '2017']

# We need to unpivot the year columns from the electricity source (df1 part)
year_cols = [str(y) for y in range(1960, 2018)]

df_elec_unpivot = df_join1.melt(
    id_vars=['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Rural Value', 'Indicator Name', 'Indicator Code'],
    value_vars=year_cols,
    var_name='Year_elec',
    value_name='Electricity Value'
)

# Now we have two year columns: 'Year' (from rural) and 'Year_elec' (from electricity)
# We need to keep rows where Year == Year_elec to align the data by year
df_elec_unpivot = df_elec_unpivot[df_elec_unpivot['Year'] == df_elec_unpivot['Year_elec']].copy()

# Drop the extra year column and Indicator columns from electricity source
df_elec_unpivot.drop(columns=['Year_elec', 'Indicator Name', 'Indicator Code'], inplace=True)

# === Second JOIN between the two unpivoted dataframes ===
# According to operation history, join again Source3_47_0 and Source3_47_1 on Country Name and Country Code
# But we already have them joined in df_elec_unpivot with Rural Value and Electricity Value aligned by year

# The final dataframe should have columns:
# ['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Rural Value', 'Electricity Value']

# Reorder columns to match target schema:
final_df = df_elec_unpivot[['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Rural Value', 'Electricity Value']].copy()

# Convert all columns to string type as per target schema
final_df = final_df.astype({
    'Country Name': 'string',
    'Country Code': 'string',
    'Year': 'string',
    'Rural Value': 'string',
    'Electricity Value': 'string'
})

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_47/target_multisource.csv"
final_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_47/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_47/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# UNPIVOT source0: from wide years columns to long format with 'Year' and 'Rural Value'
source0_long = source0.melt(
    id_vars=['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Indicator Name', 'Indicator Code'],
    var_name='Year',
    value_name='Rural Value'
)

# Filter source0_long to keep only the rural population indicator
source0_rural = source0_long[source0_long['Indicator Name'] == 'Rural population (% of total population)']

# UNPIVOT source1: from wide years columns to long format with 'Year' and 'Electricity Value'
source1_long = source1.melt(
    id_vars=['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Indicator Name', 'Indicator Code'],
    var_name='Year',
    value_name='Electricity Value'
)

# Filter source1_long to keep only the electricity access indicator
source1_electricity = source1_long[source1_long['Indicator Name'] == 'Access to electricity (% of population)']

# Join on Country Name, Country Code, and Year
joined = pd.merge(
    source0_rural[['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Rural Value']],
    source1_electricity[['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Electricity Value']],
    on=['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year'],
    how='outer'
)

# Convert Year to string to match target schema type
joined['Year'] = joined['Year'].astype(str)

# Convert values to string as target schema expects string types for values
joined['Rural Value'] = joined['Rural Value'].astype(str)
joined['Electricity Value'] = joined['Electricity Value'].astype(str)

# Write to target CSV
joined.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_47/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
